title: Incident Communication Templates (Status Page)
author: Tomáš Novák
content:
## Purpose
These templates standardize customer-facing updates on the public status page to make them (1) accurate, (2) timely, and (3) actionable.

This page provides:
- Copy-ready templates for each incident phase: Initial/Investigating, Identified, Monitoring, Resolved
- Required fields to include in every update
- Approved wording for uncertainty and partial impact
- Customer action / mitigation guidance patterns
- “Next update” timing language

**Audience:** Incident Commander (IC), Oncall SRE, and designated Comms Publisher.

---

## Principles (how we write)
1. **Be specific about impact without speculating on cause.**
   - Good: “Streaming responses are disconnecting for a subset of requests in us-east.”
   - Avoid: “Likely caused by a kernel bug” (unless confirmed + approved).
2. **Name what is impacted in customer language:** component(s), region(s), and request types.
3. **State what we know + what we don’t know.** Use approved uncertainty language (see below).
4. **Give customers something to do** when possible (retry/backoff, fallback model/region, disable streaming, etc.).
5. **Commit to a next update time** and hit it. If we miss it, post a short update acknowledging the delay and resetting expectations.
6. **No sensitive details.** Follow the disclosure policy (no customer names, exploit/vulnerability details, provider contractual details, or internal hostnames).

---

## Required fields (every update)
Include the following in every status page update (even if brief):
- **Impact:** what customers experience (errors, latency, timeouts, partial functionality)
- **Scope:** components + regions + request types affected (when known)
- **Mitigation/Workaround:** what customers can do now (or “No customer action required”)
- **Next update:** a specific timestamp or relative time (“within 30 minutes”)

**If any field is unknown**, say so explicitly. Example: “We are still determining which models are affected.”

---

## Approved uncertainty language
Use these phrases to be precise without overcommitting:
- “We are investigating reports of …”
- “We have identified the issue and are working on mitigation.”
- “We believe this affects a subset of requests … (still validating).”
- “At this time we have not observed impact to …” (avoid “not impacted” unless confident)
- “We are still determining the full scope; next update by …”

Avoid:
- “All clear” (use “Resolved” with concrete confirmation)
- “Root cause is X” before verified / approved
- “No impact” when you haven’t checked signals across regions/routes

---

## Customer guidance patterns (pick what applies)
Only include guidance that is safe and broadly applicable.

**Retry/backoff:**
- “If you are seeing errors, retry with exponential backoff.”

**Fallback models (Hosted API):**
- “If your application supports fallback models, consider temporarily routing to a compatible model variant.”

**Region routing:**
- “If you can route across regions, consider temporarily failing over from [REGION] to [REGION].”

**Streaming-specific:**
- “As a workaround, you may disable streaming and use non-streaming responses while we mitigate.”

**Rate limits / 429s:**
- “If you are receiving elevated 429s, reduce concurrency and retry with jittered backoff.”

**No action required:**
- “No customer action is required at this time. We will provide the next update by [TIME].”

Do not instruct customers to:
- Change security settings
- Expose logs that may contain sensitive data
- Perform actions that could worsen their availability without framing as optional/temporary

---

## Next update timing (how to commit)
- Always include **“Next update by [TIME]”**.
- Use the cadence guidance in **Status Page Update SLA & Cadence**. If you cannot meet the recommended cadence, set a realistic time and explain briefly.
- Format times in **UTC** on the status page. If you reference a relative time, include an absolute time as well.

Examples:
- “Next update by 18:30 UTC.”
- “Next update within 30 minutes (by 18:30 UTC).”

---

## Component + scope wording
Use customer-facing components and region names as defined in **Status Page Component Taxonomy**.

When scoping is incomplete, prefer:
- “We are investigating impact to [COMPONENT] in [REGION]. We are still validating whether other regions are affected.”

When the issue is partial (subset of traffic), prefer:
- “A subset of requests …”
- “Intermittent errors …”
- “Elevated error rate / increased latency …”

Avoid internal system names like scheduler IDs, node pools, internal service names, or cloud provider ticket numbers.

---

## Templates
Replace bracketed items like [COMPONENT], [REGION], and [TIME]. Keep updates short (2–6 sentences) unless customers need detailed guidance.

### 1) Initial / Investigating
Use when we have credible signals but no confirmed cause/mitigation yet.

**Template (Investigating):**
> **Investigating** – We are investigating an issue causing **[IMPACT]** for **[SCOPE]**.
> 
> **Impact:** [WHAT CUSTOMERS SEE] (e.g., elevated 5xx, increased latency, streaming disconnects).
> 
> **Scope:** [COMPONENT(S)] in [REGION(S)] (we are still validating full scope).
> 
> **Customer guidance:** [WORKAROUND] / “No customer action is required at this time.”
> 
> Next update by **[TIME UTC]**.

**Short form (when time is critical):**
> **Investigating** – We are investigating **[IMPACT]** affecting **[COMPONENT]** in **[REGION]**. Next update by **[TIME UTC]**.

**Examples:**
- Streaming-only:
  > **Investigating** – We are investigating an issue causing intermittent **streaming disconnects** for a subset of requests in **Hosted API – Streaming** in **us-east**. As a workaround, you may temporarily disable streaming and use non-streaming responses. Next update by **18:30 UTC**.

- Region ambiguity:
  > **Investigating** – We are investigating elevated **5xx errors** for **Hosted API – Text Generation**. We believe this is concentrated in **eu-west** but are still validating whether other regions are affected. Next update by **09:15 UTC**.

---

### 2) Identified
Use when we have a confirmed cause category and/or clear mitigation in progress.

**Template (Identified):**
> **Identified** – We have identified the cause of **[IMPACT]** affecting **[SCOPE]** and are working on mitigation.
> 
> **Impact:** [WHAT CUSTOMERS SEE + whether intermittent/partial].
> 
> **Scope:** [COMPONENT(S)] in [REGION(S)] / [MODEL FAMILY] / [ROUTE TYPE] (as applicable).
> 
> **Mitigation in progress:** [WHAT WE ARE DOING, CUSTOMER-SAFE].
> 
> **Customer guidance:** [WORKAROUND] / “No customer action is required.”
> 
> Next update by **[TIME UTC]**.

**Mitigation phrasing (approved patterns):**
- “We are rolling out a configuration change to reduce error rates.”
- “We are rebalancing capacity and routing to restore normal performance.”
- “We have paused a deployment and are reverting to the previous stable version.”

Avoid stating:
- Exact host counts, internal cluster names, kernel versions, or vulnerability-like details.

**Example (capacity/routing):**
> **Identified** – We have identified a capacity issue causing elevated **429s** for **Embeddings** requests in **us-west**. We are rebalancing capacity and adjusting routing to reduce throttling. If you are receiving 429s, reduce concurrency and retry with exponential backoff. Next update by **21:10 UTC**.

---

### 3) Monitoring
Use when mitigations are applied and we see recovery, but we are verifying stability.

**Template (Monitoring):**
> **Monitoring** – We have applied mitigation for **[IMPACT]** affecting **[SCOPE]** and are monitoring recovery.
> 
> **Current status:** [ERROR RATES/LATENCY TREND IN CUSTOMER TERMS] (e.g., “error rates have returned to near-normal levels”).
> 
> **Customer guidance:** [WORKAROUND STILL RECOMMENDED?] / “You may resume normal traffic patterns.” (only if confident)
> 
> Next update by **[TIME UTC]** (or earlier if status changes).

**Example (rollback):**
> **Monitoring** – We have reverted a deployment impacting **Hosted API – Streaming** in **us-east**. Streaming disconnect rates have decreased and are approaching normal levels; we are monitoring to confirm stability. Next update by **18:55 UTC**.

---

### 4) Resolved
Use when the incident is over and service is stable. Include a brief summary + any customer follow-ups (e.g., delayed post-incident summary).

**Template (Resolved):**
> **Resolved** – This incident has been resolved.
> 
> **Impact:** [BRIEF SUMMARY OF WHAT HAPPENED] affecting **[SCOPE]**.
> 
> **Resolution:** [CUSTOMER-SAFE DESCRIPTION OF WHAT FIXED IT].
> 
> If you continue to experience issues, please contact Support with request IDs and timestamps.

**Post-incident summary commitment (include for Sev1/Sev0):**
> We will publish a customer-facing post-incident summary within **[SLA]**.

**Example:**
> **Resolved** – This incident has been resolved. Between **17:40–18:20 UTC**, a subset of customers experienced intermittent **streaming disconnects** on **Hosted API – Streaming** in **us-east**. We mitigated the issue by reverting a configuration change and rebalancing traffic. If you continue to experience issues, please contact Support with request IDs and timestamps. We will publish a customer-facing post-incident summary within **3 business days**.

---

## Special scenarios (add-on snippets)
Use these add-ons sparingly to avoid long updates.

### A) Model-family specific impact
> Scope: We believe this primarily affects requests to **[MODEL FAMILY / MODEL NAME]**. We are validating whether other models are impacted.

### B) Dedicated / Private control plane impact
> Scope: This impacts **[Dedicated Control Plane / Private Control Plane]** operations (e.g., provisioning, scaling, rollouts). Inference request serving remains **[unaffected / potentially impacted – specify]**.

### C) Console degradation
> Customers may see delayed metrics or errors loading dashboards in the **Redwood Console**. API request serving is **[unaffected / impacted – specify]**.

### D) Ongoing mitigation after resolution (avoid overpromising)
> We have restored service and will continue follow-up work to prevent recurrence.

---

## Do / Don’t quick checklist
**Before posting, confirm:**
- Components selected match customer impact (Streaming vs API vs Embeddings vs Console, etc.)
- Region scoping is correct (global vs us-east/us-west/eu-west)
- Update includes impact + guidance + next update time
- Language matches current phase (Investigating vs Identified vs Monitoring)
- No sensitive/internal/provider-constrained details

**Escalate for review (per approval policy) if:**
- You believe the issue may be security-related
- Customer data exposure is suspected
- You need to reference a third-party provider outage in a way that could violate contracts
- You want to publish “root cause” specifics beyond a general category

---
